kind: A screen with one seed on the laptop's GPU: practice with feedback (the loop of practice_hops.json) from the two models of written_chains.json, each of which writes a chain of up to 4 hops right in at least 0.985 of lines and almost none of 6 hops.
why: written_chains.json named this screen as its next registration: both of its arms learned to chain in writing (its mark 1) and neither wrote a chain past the 4 hops it was trained on (its mark 2: at 8 hops chain-stack answers 0.105 of lines right and chain-tf 0.090, a guess among ten digits, and neither writes one whole chain right). In practice_hops.json reward could not make a model write a chain, because a model trained on direct answers almost never samples one. These two models write names after every query of two hops or more, so every attempt at the staircase's hops is a chain for the reward to grade: here the question is whether reward on the answer alone, at the edge of what a model solves, makes its written chains longer than any chain it has read. That is the step from reading reasoning written out to reasoning further than it was shown, which the one-model plan needs.
loop: experiments/practice_loop.py as in practice_hops.json: every round 16 tasks at the current number of hops, verified, 8 attempts each written as streams (the stack) or windows (the Transformer) at temperature 1.0; reward 1 if the last byte before the newline is the answer, whatever is written before it; the solve rate moves the hops by a staircase (above a half +1, below a quarter -1), starting at 4, the longest chain of the training corpus; a GRPO step (Adam at 3e-5, gradients clipped at 1) on the tasks whose attempts disagree; seed 0. Two settings differ from practice_hops.json and are fixed here: an attempt may take up to 64 bytes (--max-bytes 64, as written_chains.json measured; a written chain of 16 hops takes 47), and practice lasts 2,000 rounds (--rounds 2000), since a chain can grow by one hop a stair at most.

arms.practice-chain-stack: chain-stack's averaged weights after its 24,000 updates on the written corpus (written_chains.json)
arms.practice-chain-tf: chain-tf's averaged weights after its 24,000 updates on the written corpus

code: The frozen code copy be42570, which evaluated written_chains.json; its experiments/practice_loop.py and experiments/hop_tasks.py are those of the commit that records this. On the laptop's GPU, one arm at a time, practice-chain-stack first.
measure: Before and after practice, experiments/practice_loop.py --evaluate 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 10 12 16 --evaluate-tasks 200 --max-bytes 64 --seed 0: for every hop count 200 tasks answered greedily up to a newline or 64 bytes; the accuracy of the last byte before the newline with its 95% Wilson interval, the share of answers that write a name, the share that write the query's whole chain right (wrote_the_chain) and the mean bytes. At 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16 hops the tasks are those of written_chains.json, and the evaluation before practice must repeat that record's numbers for both arms; if any differs, the evaluation is examined before anything is read. And the rounds' log: the hops of every round, its solve rate, its mean bytes.
reading: Both bases meet written_chains.json's mark (1), so both arms are read. (a) Reward lengthens an arm's written chains if after practice its accuracy at 6 hops is at least 0.50 and at least half of its answers at 6 hops write the whole chain right (before: chain-stack 0.115 and 0.02, chain-tf 0.07 and none). (b) They reach twice the trained length if the same two marks hold at 8 hops. (c) Practice keeps what was trained if the arm's mean accuracy over 1 to 4 hops is at least 0.95 after practice (before: 0.995 and 0.991). (d) One arm practises further than the other if at 6 hops and at 8 its accuracy is at least 0.10 above the other's with the two 95% intervals apart. Reported and not read: the accuracies at 5, 7, 10, 12 and 16 hops, the rounds at each hop count, the longest chain the staircase reached and its mean hops over the last 200 rounds. One seed, synthetic: a screen of whether reward lengthens chains of thought that were first read, not a claim about reasoning in language. If neither arm meets (a), the next registration is training on written chains of more lengths (1 to 8 hops, tested to 16), which asks whether the step is learned as a step once the lengths vary.
seen_before_recording: written_chains.json and practice_hops.json with their results. Of practice from these two models: the wall time of 6 rounds and of 1 round for each arm with another seed (99) on the frozen copy, about 2 seconds a round, to set the number of rounds; their outputs were deleted unread.

result.runs: practice-chain-stack and practice-chain-tf as registered: 2,000 rounds each, seed 0, one after the other on the laptop's GPU with the frozen code copy be42570 (the stack's arm ended 2026-11-27T00:23:58Z, the Transformer's 01:55:44Z), each evaluated before and after practice at the eleven hop counts.
result.evaluator check: Passed. Before practice both arms come out at 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16 hops exactly as written_chains.json recorded chain-stack and chain-tf: the same accuracy, share of answers with a name, share of whole chains and mean bytes. So the evaluation is read.
result.reading: (a) Reward lengthened the Transformer's written chains and not the stack's. After practice practice-chain-tf answers 0.710 right at 6 hops [0.644, 0.768] and writes the whole chain right in 0.625 of its answers (0.07 and none before): both marks of 0.50 are met. practice-chain-stack answers 0.045 right at 6 hops [0.024, 0.083] and writes no whole chain (0.115 and 0.02 before): it fails. (b) Neither arm reaches twice the trained length by the mark. practice-chain-tf answers 0.605 right at 8 hops [0.536, 0.670], but the whole chain is right in 0.470 of its answers, under the 0.50 that the mark asks; practice-chain-stack answers 0.060 right at 8 hops with no whole chain. (c) Neither arm keeps what it was trained on. The mean accuracy over 1 to 4 hops falls from 0.991 to 0.508 for practice-chain-tf (0.345, 0.270, 0.605, 0.810) and from 0.995 to 0.108 for practice-chain-stack (0.205, 0.130, 0.065, 0.030), against the mark of 0.95. (d) The Transformer's arm practises further than the stack's: 0.710 against 0.045 at 6 hops and 0.605 against 0.060 at 8, more than 0.10 apart at both with the intervals apart. Reported and not read: practice-chain-tf answers 0.835 right at 5 hops (whole chain 0.770), 0.570 at 7 (0.480), 0.375 at 10 (0.220), 0.405 at 12 (0.195) and 0.345 at 16 (0.020); practice-chain-stack 0.035, 0.045, 0.045, 0.045 and 0.045 with no whole chain. The staircase reached 22 hops for the stack (round 149) and 23 for the Transformer (round 105); over the last 200 rounds the stack practised at 1 hop in every round and the Transformer at 5.34 hops on average. One seed, synthetic tasks. Since the Transformer's arm meets (a), this record's condition for training on written chains of more lengths (neither arm meets (a)) is not met, and that registration does not follow from it.

seen while reading (beside the registere.the staircase climbed to where a guess p: The staircase steps up when more than half of a round's attempts end in the right digit, whatever is written before it. From 5 hops on the digit of the line's longest chain is the answer in every one of 4,000 sampled tasks, and a digit that some name points to is right in 0.21 of the tasks at 5 hops, 0.28 at 12, 0.44 at 18 and 0.77 at 22. Both arms climbed past 20 hops within 150 rounds (a chain of 22 hops takes 65 bytes, one more than an attempt may write) with mean solve rates of 0.35 to 0.48 over the first 200 rounds, rates that such a guess can earn at those lengths. This code copy's log of the rounds does not say whether a chain was followed, so the share of guesses is not measured; what is measured is that the reward stopped asking for the chain there.
seen while reading (beside the registere.the stack's arm stopped writing chains: From about round 500 practice-chain-stack's attempts lose their form: the share of attempts that write a name falls from 1.00 (rounds 1 to 400) to 0.87, 0.64, 0.50 and 0.26 (rounds 401 to 1,200), the staircase falls to 1 hop and stays there for the last 600 rounds with a solve rate of 0.12 to 0.16 (a guessed digit of the line earns 0.15 at 1 hop), and the loss runs to -2 and -3. In a GRPO step the attempts under their task's mean push the likelihood of the model's own bytes down, and nothing bounds that push: that is the step's part that removes behaviour without naming a better one. practice-chain-tf's loss stays between -0.1 and -0.6 and it keeps writing names in 0.66 to 0.99 of its attempts.
seen while reading (beside the registere.the Transformer's arm moved its chains a: After practice practice-chain-tf is best at 5 hops (0.835) and worse the further a task is from the lengths it practised last (5.3 hops on average over the last 200 rounds). At 1 and 2 hops it answers 0.345 and 0.270 right and its answers take 41 and 46 bytes on average where a right one takes 2 and 5: the short chains it was trained on went while the longer ones came. Nothing in the loop rehearses a length that the staircase has left.
seen while reading (beside the registere.what was registered from this: practice_within_reach.json (3341a42, recorded before the Transformer's arm ended and before its rounds were read): a cap on the staircase where a guess does not pay (8 hops) and no teaching from the attempts under the mean, each alone and both, from the same two models.
